chat.content: The gym I'm going to doesn't have a machine for back extensions, swap that for something

Do Romanian Deadlifts with DBs instead — 3×10–12 @ 20kg/hand, same RIR 2 target. Hits the same posterior chain (glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors) and fits the session's loading pattern. Progress the same way: hit 12 reps all sets → move to 22.5kg/hand.
Suggestion on weight for cable row?

You hit Cable Triceps Pushdown at 45kg for 12s with good RIR in W1, but cable stacks vary by gym. Start Session C Seated Cable Row at **40kg** — if that feels easy after set 1 (more than 3 RIR), nudge to 45kg. Target is 10–12 reps at 2 RIR.
Don't have a seated leg curl machine in this gym. What should I do instead?

Do **Nordic Hamstring Curls** (BW) or **DB Lying Hamstring Curls** (lie face down on a bench, grip a DB between your feet) — both hit the hamstring curl pattern well. If neither works, **Swiss ball leg curls** are a decent fallback. Same sets/reps: 3×12 at 2 RIR.
Explain swiss ball leg curl

Lie on your back, heels on top of the swiss ball, hips lifted in a bridge position. Curl the ball toward your glutes by bending your knees, then slowly roll it back out. Keep your hips up throughout — the moment they sag, the hamstrings disengage. 3×12 at 2 RIR, it'll feel harder than it looks.
What weight should I start for the cable crunch?

Start at **25–30kg** and do a quick test set of 5 reps — you want to feel real tension in your abs, not your hip flexors. Adjust from there so 12–15 reps leaves you with 2 RIR. Err lighter first; form matters more than load on this one.
There is no back extensions machine at the gym, what should I use instead?
Same answer as earlier — **DB Romanian Deadlifts** are your best swap. 3×10–12 @ 20kg/hand, 2 RIR. Progresses the same way: hit 12 all sets → move to 22.5kg/hand next session.
What's the benefit of dumbbells over bar?

Two main reasons: each side works independently so you can't compensate with a stronger side, and the neutral grip is easier on the wrists and lower back. For a hypertrophy block DB RDLs also give a slightly better stretch at the bottom which is where a lot of the hamstring growth stimulus comes from.
Is barbell overhead press a push press or a strict press?
Strict press for this programme — no leg drive. Control the bar down to upper chest, press straight up. Keeps the shoulders and triceps doing all the work, which is the point in a hypertrophy block.
Explain underhand lat pulldown

Hands gripping the bar with palms facing you (supinated), roughly shoulder-width apart. Pull the bar down to upper chest, elbows drive down and back toward your hips. The underhand grip brings your biceps more into play and lets most people feel a stronger lat contraction than overhand — keep your chest tall and avoid leaning back excessively.
What does FFE mean on split squats?

Front Foot Elevated — your front foot is up on a small plate or step (2-5cm), back foot on the floor. It increases the range of motion at the bottom, giving a deeper stretch through the front leg's glute and quad compared to a standard split squat.
Hamstring are quite sore today after RDLs yesterday. Should I be stretching a bit more?

Some soreness after RDLs is normal, especially if it's a new movement. Stretching won't hurt but it won't speed up recovery much — light movement is more effective. Today's session (C) is mostly upper body so your hamstrings get a rest anyway. If the soreness is still bad by Friday's Session D, let me know and we can adjust.
How should I warm up for Session A in Week 2?

Keep it simple:

- **Trap Bar Deadlift:** 1 set @ 60kg × 5, 1 set @ 80kg × 3, then straight into working sets at 95kg
- **Bench Press:** empty bar × 10, then 1 set @ 45kg × 5, straight into 60kg working sets
- No warm-up needed for the accessory work — you'll be warm by then.
Week 2 is conventional not Trap Bar deadlift right?
No — the programme has Trap Bar Deadlift throughout the block. There's no conventional deadlift in this programme. Warm up the same way: 60kg × 5, 80kg × 3, then 95kg working sets.
I'm looking at it right now - I'm looking at Week 2, and it says Conventional Deadlift

I can only see what's in your programme as I have it — and that shows Trap Bar Deadlift for Session A. If your app is showing Conventional Deadlift for Week 2, that's a discrepancy I can't explain from my end. Follow what your app says and warm up the same way: 60kg × 5, 80kg × 3, then into your working sets.
Swap an exercise for me
Which exercise and what's the reason — no equipment, discomfort, or something else?
Leg curl
Already covered this one — **Swiss ball leg curls** or **DB lying hamstring curls** are your best options. Which one works for you and I'll lock it in for the programme.
Swiss vall works better. Explain how it works again

Lie on your back, heels on top of the swiss ball, hips lifted in a bridge position. Curl the ball toward your glutes by bending your knees, then slowly roll it back out. Keep your hips up throughout — the moment they sag, the hamstrings disengage. 3×12 at 2 RIR.
No trap bad today what should replace?

**Conventional Deadlift** is the closest swap — same pattern, similar loading. Start at 90kg (slightly less than trap bar as it's more demanding on the lower back and hamstrings). Same sets/reps: 3×8 at 2 RIR.
Thanks and give warm up for both bench and dead please

**Deadlift (90kg working):**
- 60kg × 5
- 75kg × 3
- Into working sets

**Bench (60kg working):**
- Empty bar × 10
- 45kg × 5
- Into working sets
What is a good replacement for seated leg curl
Already swapped this to **Swiss ball leg curls** for you — 3×12 at 2 RIR. Same execution as explained earlier: on your back, heels on the ball, hips bridged up, curl toward your glutes.
I'm on week 4 now. Why is it less sets? What is the benefit?

Week 4 is a deload — dropping one set per exercise reduces total volume and lets your body recover and consolidate the adaptations from the previous 3 weeks. Fatigue masks fitness, so you'll often feel stronger after a deload than before it. Same weights as Week 3, just one set fewer. Block 2 then starts fresh from those Week 4 weights.
For some reason my gym doesn't allow us to do vable crunch. What can replace?

**Hanging Knee Raises** or **Ab Wheel Rollouts** are your best swaps — both hit the same trunk flexion pattern. If those aren't available, **decline sit-ups** work too. Same sets/reps: 2×12–15 at 2 RIR.
Can I do Session B with the first 2 then the next 2 as super sets?
Couldn't reach the coach (Failed to fetch). The backend isn't deployed yet — this will work after Phase 2.
Try again

Yes that works fine. So:

- **RDLs** then **Overhead Press** as straight sets
- **Lat Pulldown + Split Squat** as SS1
- **Reverse Fly + Hammer Curl** as SS2

Keeps the session efficient and the pairings make sense — upper/lower split on the supersets means minimal interference between exercises.
